units.summary: The aggregate backend's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so each write is flushed to the client at once. Responses that carry a Content-Length used to be buffered, and now they are flushed per write.
units.headline: Aggregate discovery proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes ReverseProxy buffering and flushing for every response through this backend, which affects streaming and throughput.
focus: Large non-watch responses with Content-Length are now flushed per write, so check the throughput cost

units.summary: The forward backend's ReverseProxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so each write is flushed to the client at once. Watch events no longer depend on the response lacking a Content-Length.
units.headline: Forward backend proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes ReverseProxy buffering and flushing for all forwarded traffic, which affects streaming and throughput.
focus: Per-write flushing cost for large List responses through forward backends

units.summary: Adds a constant, -1, which tells ReverseProxy to flush after every write. The proxies elsewhere in this PR use it. The constant itself changes nothing at runtime.
units.headline: New streamingFlushInterval constant set to -1
units.reason: A new constant with no behavior of its own. The behavior change is in the proxies that use it.

units.summary: The breakers cache now stores the groupBreaker alias, which is the two-step breaker, instead of the one-step CircuitBreaker. This is a type change that follows the breaker.go change.
units.headline: ST fallback breaker cache uses the two-step groupBreaker type
units.reason: A type substitution that follows the breaker change. The behavior lives in breaker.go.

units.summary: The LRU for breakers is now constructed with the groupBreaker type. Only the type parameter changes.
units.headline: Breaker LRU constructed with groupBreaker type
units.reason: Only the type parameter changes, to match the struct field.

units.summary: The single-tenant fallback proxy now sets FlushInterval to -1, so each write is flushed to the client at once. Watch streaming no longer depends on the Content-Length heuristic.
units.headline: ST fallback proxy now flushes after every write
units.reason: Changes ReverseProxy flushing for all single-tenant fallback traffic, which affects streaming and throughput.
focus: Check that the new flushing interacts correctly with ModifyResponse and checkStackOrigin

units.summary: The return type changes to the groupBreaker alias. The key and lookup logic are unchanged, and callers must now use the two-step Allow API.
units.headline: breakerForDestination returns the two-step groupBreaker type
units.reason: A signature type change that follows the breaker change. The key and cache logic are untouched.
